messages:
Ryan (sales): Heads up — OmniHealth POC kicks off Mon. They want a 2-day smoke + throughput validation. Can we confirm reserved GPU preheat, autoscale policy, and an answer on the security questionnaire?
Alex (solutions): Got it. Quick Q: what's their expected request shape? tokens per req, sync vs async, embeddings vs generation?
Ryan (sales): Mostly chat/generation. Peak profile: bursts up to ~250 qps for short periods, steady ~60 qps. Median request ~100 tokens output, prompt ~40 tokens. Low embedding usage.
Alex (solutions): Ok. Rough sizing: for 100-token generation on redwood-14b-v1 we usually budget ~0.7–1.0s p50 on a 48GB A10G equiv. For burst headroom and preheat, recommend 6 reserved GPUs + autoscale to 10 for spikes. That gives ~250 qps headroom with batching.
Jen (infra): +1 to preheat. Proposed autoscale policy: keep min_reserved: 6, scale_step: 1 GPU per 30s, max: 12, scale_based_on: queued_requests and p95_latency.
Sachin (sre): Can we also use a burst credit pool rather than immediate scaling to avoid cold starts during short bursts? If burst <120s we prefer credits.
Alex (solutions): Agree. Plan: reserved pool 6, burst credits to cover additional 4 GPUs for 3 mins, autoscale kicks in if burst >3m. That minimizes cost while meeting SLO.
Ryan (sales): Sounds good. Customer asked about pricing delta if they pick quantized models.
Alex (solutions): For redwood-14b-quant (q8), expected throughput +30% with similar output quality for most prompts. We typically provide a 15% unit-price discount option in the reserved SKU if they commit to quantized model variants. I'll add numbers to the quote.
Priya (security): For the questionnaire: they asked about data isolation, KMS, SOC2, and VPC peering. Short answers: we offer VPC private deployment or VPC peering for Dedicated, KMS integration (customer-managed keys), SOC2 Type II, audit logs retention as an add-on. I need the questionnaire link to fill more detailed answers.
Ryan (sales): Pasted questionnaire here: https://omnichealth.example.com/sec-qna.pdf. They also asked about IP allowlist for admin console.
Priya (security): We support IP allowlist for console, and can enable stricter session timeouts for their account. Will prepare a formal response doc by EOD tomorrow.
Jen (infra): Ops note: to get KV cache warm for the canary traffic, prewarm steps: 1) seed common prompts into cache; 2) run synthetic warmers at 10qps for 10m; 3) verify hit rate >60%. I'll drop a small runbook snippet below.
Jen (infra): ```
# preheat-runbook (snippet)
- Step 0: deploy canary model variant (quant if agreed) to reserved pool
- Step 1: run warm generator against top-50 prompts (10qps) 10m
- Step 2: monitor kv_cache_hit_rate, p50/p95 latency
- Step 3: if hit_rate < 50% -> increase seed set; if p95 > target -> add 1 GPU
```
Sachin (sre): OpsBot: schedule smoke test for Monday 09:00 PT (canary + 2-day load validation).
OpsBot: Scheduled smoke_test_omnichealth for 2026-04-06T16:00:00Z. Canary will use reserved pool 6 + burst credits. Report will be posted in this thread. :robot_face:
Alex (solutions): I'll prepare a short deliverable: 1-pager sizing rationale, preheat runbook, pricing delta table, and a filled security checklist draft. Will drop by EOD today.
Ryan (sales): Amazing, thanks team. Can someone paste the exact autoscale JSON we'll hand to client ops?
Jen (infra): Quick JSON snippet below (for ops handoff):
Jen (infra): ```
{"autoscale": {"min_reserved": 6, "max_reserved": 12, "scale_step_secs": 30, "burst_credit_threshold_secs": 180, "metrics": ["queued_requests", "p95_latency"]}}
```
Sachin (sre): I'll attach a short tolerance table for eviction/spot fallback and SLA notes to the deliverable.
Ryan (sales): Perfect. Priya — once security doc is ready ping me and I'll loop legal. :thumbsup:
Priya (security): Will do.
Alex (solutions): Quick risk note: if they insist on 100% quantized models we may need +2 GPUs for same latency SLO due to kernel shapes; will call that out.
Ryan (sales): Good flag. If that happens, we'll reflect in quote. Thanks everyone. :pray:
